By forcing identical grid resolutions (n_x, n_y) and bounding boxes (m1, m2, M1, M2) across different players, we eliminate geometric scaling artifacts that would otherwise confound direct density comparisons. This deterministic mapping ensures all subsequent operations—convolution, interpolation, and subtraction—are performed on aligned, dimensionally consistent representations. Failure occurs when grid parameters differ, introducing spurious shifts or dilations that misrepresent relative throwing tendencies.
